blogPosts.title: How Much Does Floor Sanding Cost in Dunolly, VIC in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the real cost of professional floor sanding in Dunolly, Victoria. We break down pricing per square metre, factors that affect cost, and what to expect from your Goldfields region project.
body: If you own a home in Dunolly with timber floorboards, you have probably wondered about the cost of professional floor sanding. Whether your floors are original heritage boards from a 19th-century miner's cottage or more modern plantation hardwood, the price of sanding and finishing varies based on several key factors. In the Central Goldfields region of Victoria, homeowners typically pay between $18 and $45 per square metre for professional floor sanding and finishing, depending on the condition of the timber, the type of finish selected, and the complexity of any repairs needed. At True Blue Floors Victoria, we provide transparent, fixed-price quotes after assessing your specific floor in person at your Dunolly property.

The condition of your existing floorboards is the single biggest factor affecting the cost of floor sanding in Dunolly. Floors that have been previously finished and simply need a refresh will cost less than those with deep scratches, water damage, pet stains, or warped boards that require individual repair or replacement. In Dunolly's older homes, we frequently encounter original Victorian-era boards that have been painted over or covered with carpet for decades. These floors often need additional preparation work, including adhesive removal and board levelling, before the sanding process can begin. This extra work is reflected in the overall project cost but delivers a stunning result that adds significant value to your Dunolly home.

The type of finish you choose also plays a major role in the total cost of your Dunolly floor sanding project. Water-based polyurethane is the most popular choice for Australian homes due to its fast drying time, low odour, and excellent durability. A standard two-coat water-based finish typically costs between $18 and $28 per square metre for sand and finish combined. Oil-based polyurethane provides a richer, warmer tone but takes longer to dry and has a stronger odour during application. Premium hard wax oil finishes, which are increasingly popular in Central Victoria, start from $35 per square metre and provide a natural, matte look that is easy to maintain over time.

The size of your Dunolly floor sanding project also affects the per-square-metre price. Larger projects, such as sanding an entire house of floorboards, benefit from economies of scale because the setup and sanding equipment can run continuously across a bigger area. For a typical Dunolly weatherboard home with 80 to 120 square metres of timber flooring, you can expect to pay between $2,200 and $4,800 for a complete sand and finish. Smaller jobs, such as sanding a single room of 20 square metres, may cost slightly more per square metre due to the fixed setup costs involved. We always recommend getting a free on-site quote from True Blue Floors Victoria so we can assess your specific floor and provide an accurate price.

In Dunolly and the broader Goldfields region, the local climate also influences your floor finishing choices and costs. Central Victoria experiences hot, dry summers and cool winters with occasional frost, which means your floor finish needs to withstand significant temperature and humidity fluctuations. We recommend flexible, high-quality polyurethane finishes that can expand and contract with your timber boards without cracking or peeling. While these premium finishes may cost a few dollars more per square metre upfront, they save you money in the long run by reducing the need for early re-coating. Our team at True Blue Floors Victoria can advise you on the best finish for Dunolly's specific climate conditions.

Many Dunolly homeowners also ask about the cost of additional services such as board repair, gap filling, and floor levelling. At True Blue Floors Victoria, we can source matching timber species to replace damaged or missing boards in your Dunolly home, ensuring a seamless look across the entire floor. Gap filling between boards is typically charged at $5 to $10 per linear metre and is recommended for older homes where boards have shrunk over time. Floor levelling, which may be necessary in heritage homes where joists have settled unevenly, is quoted on a case-by-case basis. These additional services are always included in our comprehensive written quote so there are no surprises on the day.

The best way to get an accurate floor sanding price for your Dunolly home is to book a free on-site assessment with True Blue Floors Victoria. We will inspect your floorboards, discuss your finish preferences, and provide a detailed written quote that covers every aspect of the job. There are no hidden fees, no lock-in contracts, and no obligation to proceed. Call us on 0417 110 922 or email truebluefloorsanding@gmail.com to arrange your free Dunolly floor sanding quote today. We are open 24 hours and happy to work around your schedule to get your timber floors looking their absolute best.

blogPosts.title: How to Restore Original Timber Floorboards in Your Dunolly Home
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to restoring heritage timber floorboards in Dunolly's historic Goldfields homes, from initial assessment through to final finish and long-term care.
body: Dunolly is one of Victoria's oldest Gold Rush towns, and many of its homes feature original timber floorboards that are over a century old. These floorboards, often milled from local hardwood species such as red gum, stringybark, or messmate, are a beautiful and valuable feature of any Dunolly property. However, decades of use, paint layers, carpet adhesive, and general wear can leave them looking tired and worn. The good news is that virtually any original timber floorboard can be restored to its former glory with professional sanding and finishing. At True Blue Floors Victoria, we have extensive experience restoring heritage floorboards in Dunolly homes, and we love bringing these beautiful timbers back to life.

The first step in restoring your Dunolly home's original floorboards is a thorough assessment. Not all floorboards are in the same condition, and a professional inspection will identify any boards that need repair or replacement before sanding begins. In many Dunolly homes, particularly those built between 1850 and 1920, we find boards that have been damaged by termites, white ants, or moisture from leaking plumbing. These damaged boards need to be carefully removed and replaced with matching timber species before the sanding process can proceed. At True Blue Floors Victoria, we source reclaimed and new hardwood timber that matches the species and age of your original Dunolly floorboards for a seamless, authentic result.

Before any sanding begins, all furniture and fittings need to be removed from the room. Many Dunolly homeowners choose to handle this themselves, but True Blue Floors Victoria can also arrange assistance if needed. Once the room is clear, we begin the sanding process using our dust-controlled sanding systems. These machines capture up to 98 percent of the dust generated during sanding, which is particularly important in Dunolly's older homes where dust can settle into ceiling cavities and wall spaces. The sanding process typically involves three passes with progressively finer sandpaper, starting with a coarse 24-grit to remove the old finish and ending with a fine 100-grit for a smooth, ready-to-finish surface.

One of the most rewarding aspects of restoring original floorboards in a Dunolly home is discovering the beautiful timber hidden beneath layers of paint, varnish, or carpet. We have uncovered stunning red gum boards in Dunolly miner's cottages that had been hidden under carpet for over 50 years. The rich red and brown tones of these native Victorian hardwoods are truly spectacular once revealed through professional sanding. If your Dunolly home's floorboards have been painted, the sanding process will carefully remove all paint layers to expose the natural timber grain beneath. This transformation is one of the reasons Dunolly homeowners love the floor restoration process.

After sanding is complete, the next critical step is applying the right finish to protect your Dunolly floorboards for years to come. In Central Victoria's dry climate, we recommend water-based polyurethane for its flexibility, fast drying time, and excellent UV resistance. Most Dunolly homes benefit from two to three coats of polyurethane, with light sanding between coats to ensure proper adhesion. For a more natural, matte appearance, hard wax oil is an excellent alternative that penetrates the timber rather than sitting on top of it. Whatever finish you choose, the team at True Blue Floors Victoria will ensure your Dunolly floorboards are sealed and protected against everyday wear and tear.

The cost of restoring original floorboards in a Dunolly home depends on the size of the area, the condition of the boards, and the finish selected. For a typical Dunolly weatherboard with 80 to 100 square metres of original hardwood floorboards, restoration costs generally range from $2,800 to $5,500. This includes board repair, full sanding, and three coats of premium polyurethane finish. While this is a significant investment, it is far less than the cost of ripping out old floors and installing new timber flooring, which can exceed $80 per square metre installed. Restoring your original Dunolly floorboards is also the more sustainable choice, as it preserves the existing timber and avoids the environmental impact of manufacturing new flooring products.

If you are ready to restore the original timber floorboards in your Dunolly home, True Blue Floors Victoria is here to help. We offer free on-site assessments and detailed written quotes for all Dunolly floor restoration projects. Our dust-controlled sanding systems, premium Australian finishes, and decades of experience with heritage Goldfields homes make us the obvious choice for your floorboard restoration project. Call us on 0417 110 922 or email truebluefloorsanding@gmail.com to arrange your free assessment today. We are open 24 hours and ready to bring your Dunolly floorboards back to life.

blogPosts.title: Best Floor Finishes for Central Victorian Homes: A Complete Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing the right floor finish for your Dunolly home? Compare polyurethane, oil, and hard wax options for Central Victorian climate conditions.
body: Choosing the right finish for your timber floorboards is one of the most important decisions you will make during a floor sanding project in Dunolly. The finish not only determines the look and feel of your floor, but also its durability, maintenance requirements, and resistance to the unique climate conditions of Central Victoria. Dunolly experiences hot, dry summers with temperatures regularly exceeding 35 degrees, cool winters with overnight frost, and low humidity throughout much of the year. These conditions cause timber to expand and contract significantly, which means your floor finish must be flexible enough to move with the wood without cracking, peeling, or wearing prematurely.

Water-based polyurethane is the most popular floor finish in Australian homes, and for good reason. It dries quickly, has low odour during application, and provides excellent durability against foot traffic and everyday wear. For Dunolly homeowners, water-based polyurethane is an ideal choice because it remains flexible in the face of Central Victoria's temperature and humidity swings. It is available in a range of sheen levels from high gloss to matte, allowing you to customise the look of your Dunolly floor to suit your interior design. At True Blue Floors Victoria, we typically apply two to three coats of water-based polyurethane for maximum protection, with the number of coats depending on the level of foot traffic in your Dunolly home.

Oil-based polyurethane has been used on timber floors in Australia for decades and remains a popular choice for Dunolly homeowners who prefer a richer, warmer finish. Oil-based finishes amber over time, giving your floor a golden, honey-toned appearance that many people find attractive in heritage Dunolly homes. However, oil-based polyurethane takes significantly longer to dry between coats, has a stronger chemical odour during application, and is less environmentally friendly than water-based alternatives. For these reasons, we generally recommend water-based finishes for most Dunolly projects, but oil-based finishes can be an excellent choice for specific heritage restoration projects where an authentic, aged appearance is desired.

Hard wax oil is a premium floor finish that has gained popularity in recent years among discerning Dunolly homeowners. Unlike polyurethane, which forms a protective film on top of the timber, hard wax oil penetrates into the wood and hardens within the grain. This creates a natural, matte finish that showcases the true beauty and texture of your Dunolly floorboards. The major advantage of hard wax oil is that it is easy to spot-repair if scratched or damaged, as you simply sand the affected area and re-apply the oil without needing to refinish the entire floor. For Dunolly homes with heritage floorboards, hard wax oil provides an authentic, traditional look that complements period architecture beautifully.

In Dunolly's dry Central Victorian climate, one of the key considerations when choosing a floor finish is UV resistance. Prolonged exposure to direct sunlight can cause timber floors to fade or change colour over time, and this effect is amplified in the Goldfields region where summer sun is intense. High-quality water-based polyurethanes with UV inhibitors provide the best protection against sun damage for your Dunolly floorboards. We also recommend using curtains or blinds in rooms with large north-facing windows to reduce direct UV exposure during peak summer months. At True Blue Floors Victoria, we can advise Dunolly homeowners on the best combination of finish and UV protection for their specific property and orientation.

Maintenance requirements also vary significantly between floor finishes, and this is an important consideration for Dunolly families. Water-based polyurethane floors are the easiest to maintain, requiring regular sweeping and occasional damp mopping with a pH-neutral cleaner. Hard wax oil floors need a little more attention, including periodic re-application of maintenance oil in high-traffic areas such as hallways and kitchens. Oil-based polyurethane floors are durable but can be difficult to repair locally if scratched, as the finish does not blend easily. For busy Dunolly households with children and pets, we generally recommend a satin-finish water-based polyurethane for the best combination of durability, appearance, and ease of maintenance.

Selecting the right floor finish for your Dunolly home does not have to be overwhelming. The team at True Blue Floors Victoria will walk you through all the options during your free on-site assessment, providing samples and expert advice tailored to your specific Dunolly property. We only use Australian-made, low-VOC finishes that meet Australian Standards for indoor air quality, ensuring your family's safety and comfort. Whether you prefer the classic warmth of oil-based polyurethane, the modern versatility of water-based coatings, or the natural elegance of hard wax oil, we have the expertise to deliver a beautiful, long-lasting result for your Dunolly floorboards.

blogPosts.title: 5 Signs Your Dunolly Timber Floors Need Professional Sanding
blogPosts.excerpt: Not sure if your Dunolly home's timber floorboards need sanding? Learn the key warning signs that it is time to call a professional.
body: Timber floorboards are one of the most durable and beautiful flooring options in Dunolly homes, but even the toughest hardwood needs periodic maintenance to keep looking its best. Over time, daily foot traffic, furniture movement, pet claws, and UV exposure can take a toll on your floor's finish, leaving it looking dull, scratched, and worn. Professional floor sanding removes the damaged top layer of finish and a thin layer of timber, revealing fresh, unblemished wood beneath that can be refinished to look brand new. But how do Dunolly homeowners know when it is time to call in the professionals? Here are five key signs that your Dunolly home's timber floorboards are overdue for a professional sand and finish.

The first and most obvious sign that your Dunolly floorboards need sanding is visible scratching and surface damage. Light surface scratches from everyday foot traffic and moving furniture are normal, but when scratches become deep enough to catch your fingernail, they have penetrated through the finish and into the timber itself. In Dunolly homes with children, pets, or heavy foot traffic in hallways and entryways, deep scratches can appear within just a few years of a previous finish. If you notice clusters of deep scratches across your Dunolly floorboards, particularly in high-traffic areas, it is time to consider professional sanding. True Blue Floors Victoria can remove these scratches and restore a smooth, even surface to your Dunolly floors.

The second sign is a dull, lifeless appearance that no amount of cleaning can fix. When your timber floorboards were first finished, they had a rich, vibrant appearance with a subtle sheen that enhanced the natural beauty of the timber grain. Over time, the protective finish wears thin, and your Dunolly floors begin to look flat and dull. If you find yourself mopping and cleaning your floors frequently but they still do not look clean or shiny, the finish has likely worn through and the timber itself is exposed. This exposed timber is vulnerable to moisture damage, staining, and further deterioration. A professional sand and finish from True Blue Floors Victoria will restore the vibrant, healthy appearance of your Dunolly floorboards.

The third sign to watch for is discolouration or staining that has set into your Dunolly floorboards. Sunlight, water spills, pet accidents, and general wear can all cause your timber floors to develop dark spots or uneven colour over time. In Dunolly's older homes, we often see significant discolouration in rooms that receive direct afternoon sun from the west, where UV exposure has bleached or darkened the timber unevenly. Water stains from leaking plumbing or wet umbrellas are another common issue in Goldfields region homes. While some surface staining can be improved with cleaning, deep-set stains that have penetrated into the timber can only be fully removed through professional sanding. The team at True Blue Floors Victoria can assess your Dunolly floorboards and determine which stains can be sanded out.

The fourth sign is peeling, bubbling, or flaking of your existing floor finish. This typically indicates that the previous coating has lost its adhesion to the timber surface, often due to moisture, poor application, or incompatibility between finish layers. In Dunolly homes, peeling finishes are common in areas near bathrooms, laundries, and kitchens where moisture levels fluctuate. You may notice small flakes of finish accumulating in corners or along the edges of the room, or you may see bubbling or blistering in the middle of the floor. These issues will only worsen over time if left untreated, as moisture continues to get beneath the compromised finish and damage the timber. Professional sanding removes the failing finish entirely and allows True Blue Floors Victoria to apply a fresh, properly bonded coating to your Dunolly floors.

The fifth and final sign that your Dunolly floorboards need professional sanding is squeaking, creaking, or uneven boards. While squeaking is primarily a structural issue related to the subfloor and joists, it often becomes apparent when the floor finish wears thin and timber boards begin to move against each other or against the fixings. In Dunolly's older heritage homes, settling of the building's foundations over many decades can cause uneven floorboards that create trip hazards and unsightly gaps. During a professional sanding project, True Blue Floors Victoria can identify and address these structural issues, including securing loose boards, filling gaps, and levelling uneven areas to ensure your Dunolly floor is both beautiful and safe for your family.

If you have noticed any of these five signs in your Dunolly home, it is time to arrange a professional floor assessment with True Blue Floors Victoria. We provide free on-site inspections for Dunolly homeowners, during which we assess the condition of your floorboards, identify any underlying issues, and provide a detailed written quote for the recommended work. Our dust-controlled sanding systems minimise mess and disruption, and we use only premium Australian-made finishes that are designed to withstand Central Victoria's demanding climate. Call us on 0417 110 922 or email truebluefloorsanding@gmail.com to arrange your free Dunolly floor assessment today. We are open 24 hours and ready to help bring your timber floors back to life.
